projects.title: Russian Industry
projects.subtitle: Interactive installations · Russia Expo
projects.goal: The country has ambitious plans for shipbuilding: a new generation of civilian vessels, breakthrough engineering, the modernization of the industry and the training of its specialists. All of it had to reach the wide audience of Russia Expo — spectacular and easy to follow.
projects.solution: We built a fully immersive exhibition. Visitors examine the flagship projects and the new ships in three dimensions, take them apart unit by unit and see where the industry’s innovation actually sits. Complex technology turns into a clear, gripping story — one the visitor lives through firsthand.

text: Over eight months the “Made by Us” pavilion drew more than 2 million visitors, for whom over 81,000 guided tours were run. Through the interactive exhibits a vast audience got to know contemporary Russian industry — from shipbuilding achievements to the workings of the national “Chestny ZNAK” product-marking system.

Children and young people got particular attention. In the Hall of the Future visitors explored modern industrial professions and literally tried them on, building their own images of the specialists of tomorrow. Complex industrial subjects turned into a personal experience — emotional, interactive and memorable.

projects.title: Russian Airports
projects.subtitle: International airports · Russia Expo
projects.goal: Present three of Russia’s international airports at Russia Expo so that each one reveals its own architecture and character — and turn the encounter into a lively experience that works for visitors of any age.
projects.solution: In a single space at Russia Expo we presented three international airports — each with its own architectural signature and its own installation. At Yelizovo, visitors colored a paper plane and launched it over the Kamchatka terminal. At Simferopol, they flew a paper plane through the terminal with a wave of the hand. At Gelendzhik, a gesture repainted the terminal’s living LED ceiling. Three buildings, three ways to feel what makes them different.

text: “Russia in Motion” was seen by more than 600,000 visitors. Three interactive installations introduced a vast audience to the airports of Yelizovo, Gelendzhik and Simferopol — their architecture, their development and their place in the country’s transport system.

Instead of being told about the airports, visitors engaged with them directly: building and launching aircraft, controlling the architectural lighting, exploring the space through game mechanics. From the virtual Yelizovo airport alone guests performed 40,000 take-offs. Infrastructure projects became a personal experience, and the airports gained live contact with an audience — including through a period when some of them were temporarily closed to passengers.

flow.text: [1] Yelizovo Airport (Kamchatka)

An interactive installation that makes the visitor a co-author. You take a sheet of paper printed with the outline of a plane, color it in and place it on a dedicated table. On the screen a digital model of the plane assembles itself in augmented reality — in exactly the design the visitor has just drawn. The plane takes off and flies over the terminal of Yelizovo Airport. The surroundings are rebuilt from real cartographic data. Rendering runs on Unreal Engine 5; three cameras read the drawing.
[2] Simferopol Airport

An interactive game, Paper Plane Flight. The visitor steps up to the booth, reaches out a hand — and a paper plane appears on the screen. Steering the flight with gestures, the player crosses the space of the terminal, collects bonuses and completes in-game tasks. The terminal is rendered in realistic graphics on Unreal Engine 5.
[3] Gelendzhik Airport

The interactive zone of Gelendzhik Airport. The visitor steps into a ring of light and sees the airport interiors from a range of angles on the screen ahead. Waving their arms, they drive the visual environment and watch the terminal’s living LED ceiling — an intricate color-lighting system — change in real time.

projects.title: UEC UAC
projects.subtitle: Dynamic exhibition space · MAKS 2021
projects.goal: MAKS, the International Aviation and Space Salon, is one of the world’s major aerospace events. United Engine Corporation (UEC), Russia’s leading developer of aircraft engines, was presenting its pavilion there.
projects.solution: For the UEC booth we built a multimedia immersion into the world of aircraft engine manufacturing. A complex screen setup, one shared rhythm across every image and a set of interactive experiences turn the pavilion into a single living space where the technology reads at a glance.

figures.label: visitors to MAKS-2021 over six days
Best Pavilion at the air show

text: The multimedia exhibition put UEC’s most demanding engineering into a language that is clear and worth watching — from the PD-14 and the forthcoming PD-35 to a new generation of aero engines. Over six days MAKS-2021 drew more than 135,000 visitors, and the UEC exhibition itself won the air show’s special award for Best Pavilion.

Technology normally reserved for engineers and industry specialists became legible to a broad audience through visual storytelling and multimedia experience. The exhibition worked on three fronts at once: demonstrating technological leadership, making Russian engine-building known beyond the industry, and drawing a new generation towards aviation and engineering professions.

projects.title: Proryv
projects.subtitle: Rosatom · the presentation tunnel
projects.goal: Build an installation that shows in plain visual terms how a nuclear power platform with a closed nuclear fuel cycle based on fast neutrons actually works.
projects.solution: An informational multimedia installation about the Proryv technologies. A complex screen setup and the tunnel effect create the sensation of moving through space and pull the viewer bodily into the story. The piece works as a visual ride and becomes the spot everyone photographs and films.

text: At the IV Congress of Young Scientists the “Perpetual Motion” installation became one of the focal points for delegates and press alike. Over three days the Congress gathered more than 7,000 people from 62 countries, and the intricate principles of next-generation nuclear power found a form that was both clear and striking.

The space, drawn from the geometry of a nuclear fuel assembly, worked as an educational instrument and a strong visual image at the same time. Visitors got to know the closed nuclear fuel cycle, examined the technology at engineering level, and photographed and filmed the installation. Six television companies used it in their reports, and the photographs and video carried the story of the Proryv project on well beyond the Congress.

projects.title: Rostec Expo
projects.subtitle: Holographic catalog
projects.goal: Create the centerpiece exhibit at the entrance to the Rostec Expo pavilion and bring the products of every company in the Rostec group together in one holographic space.
projects.solution: A holographic installation shaped like the Rostec logo. The transparent screen keeps the hall visible through it, while a control console opens the group’s full product catalog — all inside a single holographic space.

text: The holographic cube became the centrepiece of Rostec Expo and is still in service years after launch. It presents the work of the corporation’s enterprises, hosts presentations for partners and introduces visiting delegations to Rostec’s technological capabilities.

The installation turned from an exhibition piece into a permanent communication tool: presentations and important meetings begin here, and complex technology takes on a form that is both striking and clear. One object keeps working across different companies, products and scenarios — the content changes while the system itself remains part of the pavilion’s infrastructure.

projects.title: PTK Group
projects.subtitle: Exhibition installation
projects.goal: PTK Group builds modern track machines — equipment for constructing, repairing and maintaining railways. Almost all of it shares one trait: it is long and drawn out.
projects.solution: We turned that trait into the format itself. The content was made for an ultra-wide screen on the booth that echoes the proportions of the machines. The display follows the shape of the product: each machine unfolds horizontally at full length, and its structure and specifications read clearly.

projects.title: MiG-35 Booth
projects.subtitle: Multimedia booth at the MAKS 2019 airshow
projects.goal: Make the MiG-35 stand out among the other manufacturers’ aircraft, and build a demonstration tool for presenting the jet to customers.
projects.solution: We designed a plinth and a load-bearing structure for the aircraft and installed an LED screen. The screen ran purpose-built 3D content laying out the key characteristics of the MiG-35. The plinth, the large structure above it and 50 sq m of screen set the jet apart.

flow.caption: LED screen content, 15 meters across the front

flow.text: Graphics
We had 15 days to produce the content. In that time we developed and pitched several visual directions. Final resolution of the video content: 6000 × 1800 px.
How the booth was designed

After a round of sketches we settled on a design with a plinth for the aircraft, a load-bearing structure and an LED screen. Sunlight calculations showed that a canopy was needed to raise the contrast of the image on the screen. The structure is built from Layher truss elements and wrapped in fully printed banner fabric.

flow.text: Aircraft livery

To get the strongest presentation effect we developed a special livery — the paint design of the aircraft. The painting process set the limits: two colors, light blue and white, applied through stencils.

projects.title: Panorama 360
projects.subtitle: Mobile guide in augmented reality
projects.client: Panorama 360 · Moscow City observation deck, Federation Tower
projects.goal: Give visitors to one of Europe’s highest observation decks — Panorama 360, on the 89th floor of the Federation Tower in Moscow City — a new way to read the city.
projects.solution: We built a guide in augmented reality. Point a tablet at the panorama beyond the window and markers appear above the city, pinned to its landmarks. Tap one and its story opens: archive and present-day photographs, panoramas and an audio narration in Russian, English and Chinese. Moscow’s landmark buildings and places, historical and contemporary, unfold right on top of the real view.

[2] Twelve illuminated AR markers are set around the deck: point a device at one and a 3D model of a Moscow City skyscraper grows on the screen, with information about it.

projects.title: Urban Forum 2018
projects.subtitle: Multimedia booth for the Moscow City Government
projects.goal: A booth for a city government that speaks to residents in their own language — by showing plainly what is changing in the city.
projects.solution: We built a 100 sq m interactive pavilion. Six multimedia installations tell the story of the capital’s new initiatives in the voices of the people who live there. A media facade with 3D graphics, a scale model of Moscow with augmented reality and live infographics turn municipal data into an experience that is clear and worth staying for.

flow.caption: The pavilion film, Moscow Urban Forum

flow.text: The project ran in four stages

items: Project concept
Developing the installations and producing the visual content
Building the booth, installing the multimedia equipment
Commissioning and on-site support during the event

flow.text: Developing the concept for the installations

While the pavilion concept was taking shape we gathered material from five departments of the Moscow City Government. The data was sorted by topic and prioritized, and the Playdisplay creative team then formulated a set of multimedia solutions to carry the messages and the facts.
Graphics on the media facade

The media facade screened off the interior of the pavilion, which gave the hologram ideal conditions. The screen played a purpose-made 3D film — a composite architectural portrait of contemporary Moscow. Animated infographics and the headline figures ran over it as a separate layer.
Scale model with augmented reality

At the front of the booth stood a scale model with augmented reality — a composite architectural image of Moscow: the towers of Moscow City, the VDNH park, the technology parks. With a tablet in hand, visitors could see information about the projects of the Moscow City Government and the results achieved.

flow.caption: The Moscow city model in augmented reality

projects.title: Password to Victory: Stalingrad
projects.subtitle: Panoramic projection hall
projects.client: Battle of Stalingrad Museum and Memorial Complex
projects.goal: Draw public attention to a heritage site of federal significance and tell the story of the Battle of Stalingrad of 1942–1943 accurately — as an instrument of patriotic education and of keeping historical memory alive.
projects.solution: Full immersion built from light, sound and historical reconstruction: projection rebuilds pre-war Stalingrad and carries the viewer into the battle. A quiet but powerful space, where you live the history of your own city instead of reading it. Attendance at the museum doubled after the hall opened.

flow.text: The project is devoted to the final phase of the Battle of Stalingrad — the capture of the headquarters of the German 6th Army in the building of the Central City Department Store. It recreates the atmosphere of the events on the Square of Fallen Fighters in Stalingrad in 1942–1943, one of the epicenters of the largest battle on the Volga.

projects.title: COALCO Dry Port
projects.subtitle: Interactive installation and 3D film
projects.goal: The dry port is on such a scale that it only makes sense shown whole: how this new transport and logistics hub outside Moscow is put together, how its key systems work, and how it changes freight across the region.
projects.solution: This is not a film but a step-by-step installation under the viewer’s control. You drive the presentation yourself, examine the hub’s key points in 3D graphics with a full 360° view, and see the architecture, the traffic and the rhythm of the port at work — along with its geopolitical role on a three-dimensional world map.

projects.title: Sinara Transport Machines
projects.subtitle: Holographic cubes · machinery manufacturing
projects.goal: Sinara Transport Machines builds a new generation of locomotives. The task was to show not only the machines but the way the company works: design, testing on digital twins, production.
projects.solution: Three holographic cubes, linked into one narrative, walk the viewer through the entire cycle — from the design office to the shop floor to service. New industrial processes call for a new way of showing them: the hologram lays digital graphics over real scale models, and complex technology becomes tangible.

flow.text: About holograms

A hologram is an image of a three-dimensional object that comes remarkably close to the object itself. A true projection onto thin air is not yet possible: a hologram needs a surface for the light to fall on. We reproduce the effect inside a closed volume with a system of mirrors — we call that setup a holocube.

projects.title: Cosmonautics and Aviation Center
projects.subtitle: An exhibition of 115 touchscreens · VDNH
projects.goal: Tell the history of spaceflight and rocketry through high-technology solutions.
projects.solution: We delivered an exhibition of 115 touchscreens and the installation The History of Human Spaceflight for the United Rocket and Space Corporation at the Cosmonautics and Aviation Center.

flow.text: One information system

A single information system runs alongside every exhibit at the Cosmonautics and Aviation Center at VDNH. Visitors work it through the installation interface, and it gives them almost any fact about space and about what humanity has achieved beyond our planet.
For this task we developed a dedicated visual language and graphic interface.
